title: Boundary Of Binary Tree
statement:
The boundary of a binary tree is the root, followed by the left boundary from top to bottom, then all leaves from left to right, then the right boundary from bottom to top. Exclude leaves from both side boundaries so each leaf appears once. A single-node tree has boundary `[root.val]`. The root is not considered a leaf for purposes of the general concatenation.

The left boundary follows the left child when available, otherwise the right child, and excludes leaves. The right boundary follows the right child when available, otherwise the left child, and excludes leaves.

## Examples

```text
Input: root = [1,null,2,3,4]
Output: [1,3,4,2]
```

```text
Input: root = [1,2,3,4,5,6,null,null,null,7,8,9,10]
Output: [1,2,4,7,8,9,10,6,3]
```

## Constraints

- The number of nodes is in `[1, 10^4]`
- `-1000 <= Node.val <= 1000`
